title: Victoria Sponge
subtitle: The classic British sandwich cake
excerpt: Two light, even sponge layers filled with strawberry jam and whipped cream. A well-made Victoria sponge rises evenly, feels springy when pressed, and has a golden, paper-thin crust.

recipe.sourceNotes: Victoria sponge is named after Queen Victoria, who was said to enjoy a slice of sponge cake with her afternoon tea. The recipe in its current form uses the all-in-one or creaming method, both of which appear in British baking books from the mid-nineteenth century onward.

recipeTools.notes: For creaming the butter and sugar.
Two matching tins for the two layers.

content.text: Victoria sponge is two even sponge cakes made by the creaming method, filled with strawberry jam and whipped cream. The crumb is light and tender and the sponges should be exactly the same height. Getting that consistency comes down to weighing the batter evenly between the two tins and watching the oven carefully.
Heat the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4. Grease two 20 cm round cake tins and line the bases with baking paper.
Beat the butter and caster sugar together with an electric mixer on high speed for 4 to 5 minutes until very pale and fluffy. Scrape down the bowl halfway through.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating well between each addition. Add the vanilla. If the mixture starts to curdle, add a tablespoon of flour.
Sift the flour and baking powder over the batter. Add the milk. Fold in gently with a large spoon until just combined. Do not overmix.

Divide the batter evenly between the two tins, weighing them on a scale to be sure. Smooth the tops. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden, springy when pressed in the centre, and pulling away from the sides. A skewer inserted in the centre should come out clean.
Cool in the tins for 5 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack. Leave to cool completely before filling.
Spread the jam over the flat side of one sponge. Spread the whipped cream on top. Place the second sponge on top, crust-side up. Dust with icing sugar.
